verdicts.one_liner: Quotes accurate: problem_io says 'imaginary part', step description says 'obtain chi''', but docstring says 'NEGATIVE of the imaginary part' and background gives -chi''=pi[S(w)-S(-w)]; test 4 asserts chi[w>0.1]>0, so targets encode -chi''. Real contradiction, docstring side wins; minor is right.

Description only says 'set a fill value of 0' with no interpolation scheme; omega=linspace(-0.2,2.0,10) (step ~0.244) makes -omega off-grid so a scheme is required; linear is the scipy/numpy default and deps import scipy.interpolate, so minor (not major) is correctly calibrated.

Docstring says V_eff in 'inverse of square angstrom', but with 4*pi*e^2=1 and q,kappa in inverse angstrom, V_eff=1/(q^2+kappa^2) is angstrom^2 — label is dimensionally inverted; no score impact, minor doc fix.

summary: All 3 findings confirmed by reading (Tier A): the chi-sign wording contradiction in 48.4, the unstated linear-interpolation convention in 48.4, and the inverted unit label in 48.2 docstring. All minor, doc/prompt edits; problem is fair to score as-is.
